# Triangle scale identity and an actual quadrilateral obstruction

Keep the canonical balanced normals `(1,0),(0,1),(-1,-1)`. Let k be
area, Q_i the three through-source cap areas, sigma_i their coarea
lengths, M=sum Q_i/sigma_i, and f_i=2sqrt(kQ_i)/(sigma_i M).

For a triangle with strict distinct-vertex incidence, put H=2M and use
the exact cube parameters u_i from
`candidate d61c49578c90db6d`. Write
P=u_1u_2u_3 and R=(1-u_1)(1-u_2)(1-u_3). Then

    2k/H^2=P+R,
    f_1f_2f_3=8sqrt(PR),
    k/M^2-f_1f_2f_3/2=2(sqrt(P)-sqrt(R))^2.       (1)

For the first identity, divide all vertex margins by H. The two edge
vectors from vertex 1 to vertices 2 and 3 have, up to simultaneous sign,
coordinates

    (u_1,-(1-u_3)),  (1-u_2,u_2+u_3-1).

Their determinant is
`1-sum u_i+sum_(i<j)u_i u_j=P+R`. It is positive on the actual cube-slab
domain. The remaining identities follow from the exact products for f.
In particular the scale inequality

    M sigma_1 sigma_2 sigma_3 >=4sqrt(k Q_1Q_2Q_3)    (2)

holds for every such triangle, with equality precisely at cubic equality.
Unlike f, the scale k/M^2 must retain the determinant normalization of
the chosen normals; (1)--(2) here use the stated canonical pair.

Inequality (2) is FALSE for general quadrilaterals. An exact example is

    K=conv{(-10,3),(2,-6),(5,10),(-2,9)}

at source zero with the same normals. Its consecutive turns and its
oriented edge-to-origin determinants are all positive, so it is an
actual convex quadrilateral with an interior source. Direct clipping gives

    k=253/2,
    Q=(369/7,793/8,1012/19),
    sigma=(193/14,73/8,164/19),
    M=12048360/577649.

All these quantities are positive, and the exact squared gap is

    (M sigma_1 sigma_2 sigma_3)^2-16k Q_1Q_2Q_3
        =-891738498096/17689 <0.

Thus the extra triangle scale identity cannot be imposed on unrestricted
quadrilaterals. Here Q_2/k=793/1012>1/2, so this certificate makes no claim
about a version with an additional small-cap ceiling. It is not a
counterexample to the cubic inequality or to mixed-integer depth.
